ARCHMAT trains scientists and humanists together in archaeometry — the physico-chemical analysis of archaeological and heritage materials — coordinated from the University of Évora. The 2026-2028 round is under evaluation, and the next call is expected to open in November with a February scholarship deadline, following the programme's usual cycle.

Programme Highlights

  • Science-plus-humanities programme in archaeological materials analysis
  • November-February application pattern across cycles
  • Lab training in the leading European heritage-science centres
  • Careers in conservation science, museums and heritage research

Who Should Apply

Graduates in chemistry, physics, geology, materials science, archaeology and conservation are all welcomed — the programme explicitly bridges the two cultures.

Funding and Costs

Erasmus Mundus scholarships for selected students: participation costs plus monthly allowance.

Deadline and How to Apply

Track the ARCHMAT site (now hosted at Évora) for the 2027-2029 call and prepare the standard document set plus any portfolio items. Key deadline information: Annual cycle: applications open in November with a scholarship deadline around February — 2027-2029 dates on the official page.
